wrapper_sv:
`timescale 1ns/1ps

/* expose the recovered package pins through the documented interface. */
module crypto_dut (
    input wire SCK,
    input wire RST_N,
    input wire MOSI,
    input wire NORM_CS_N,
    input wire START,
    input wire ENC_DEC,
    output wire MISO,
    output wire BUSY,
    output wire ICE_LED
);
    /* preserve the recovered core and its package-pin connections. */
    recovered recovered_core (
        .pin_36(SCK),
        .pin_34(RST_N),
        .pin_32(MOSI),
        .pin_31(MISO),
        .pin_28(NORM_CS_N),
        .pin_27(START),
        .pin_25(ENC_DEC),
        .pin_38(BUSY),
        .pin_23(ICE_LED)
    );
endmodule
scheduling_explanation:
initialize_interface runs once at time zero and sets SCK low; MOSI=0 and ENC_DEC=0 are explicit testbench defaults. Thereafter sck_pulse is the only SCK writer. Every operation changes controls while SCK is low, then sck_pulse waits 10 us before raising SCK. It samples MISO and BUSY 1 ns later, after nonblocking assignments have settled, waits the remaining 9.999 us, and lowers SCK. Consecutive rising edges are exactly 20 us apart, with no background clock or interrupt handler. A reentrancy guard rejects overlapping pulse ownership.

The recovered MISO pin is a register updated on the rising edge from the pre-shift serial state. Sampling 1 ns after that edge observes the outgoing bit after its NBA update, while MOSI is shifted on the same edge. This produces exactly 32 samples for 32 clocks without dropping or inserting a bit. A pre-edge MISO sample would see the previous registered output. BUSY is checked for X/Z before every use; received and expected words also reject X/Z explicitly.

Real Icarus runs corrected the proposed wrapper mapping: NORM_CS_N is pin_28 and ENC_DEC is pin_25, with all other proposed connections unchanged. The original proposed swap passed an echo but produced c359c3ff instead of the encryption vector; the corrected wrapper passes echo, 59c359c3 -> 9cd84392 encryption, and 9cd84392 -> 59c359c3 decryption without changing recovered_sim.v.

Both measured BUSY traces are e0=1, e1=1, e2=1, e3=0, e4=0, e5=0, e6=0, e7=0. The baseline still supplies all seven post-start pulses in both modes; those observations do not justify shortening the replay or establish the exact result-load edge. Fixed mode never exits early. Bounded completion mode continues emitting SCK pulses until BUSY is known low or a caller-supplied 1..64-pulse limit expires. Invalid inputs, unknown values, mismatches, and timeout paths emit FAIL and $fatal(1,...).

The baseline uses 180 pulses and eight counted checks. Each separately reset random SPI echo adds 66 pulses and two checks, with no inferred cryptographic oracle. A fixed 32-bit LCG uses +seed=<unsigned decimal>, default 4313; +random_trials defaults to 8 and is limited to 0..64. A separate 100 ms simulation watchdog exceeds the 88.08 ms maximum valid run but bounds all execution. Real runs passed with 0 and 8 random trials at seed 4313, 64 trials at seed 4294967295, and one trial at seed 0. All output waveforms are written to waveforms.vcd.
